title: Arms In? Angular Momentum Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A skater spins faster as she pulls her arms in. A diver curls into a ball and flips faster. Nobody pushes them, yet their spin speeds up. And when Diya tries it on a spinning chair, she suddenly whirls around. Where does the extra spin come from? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the conservation of angular momentum.

On a live motion notebook Diya, seen from above, pulls two weights in from 0.8 m to 0.2 m while the readout tracks r, I, omega, L and spin energy, and a graph shows the L line staying flat while omega climbs. A slow-mo replay freezes mid-pull: her pull points at the axis, so its torque is zero. We reason link by link why omega must triple, build L = I omega, dL/dt = torque and I1 omega1 = I2 omega2 step by step, and answer two pause-and-think questions: does her spin energy change, and does letting go of the weights speed her up? Then a ring dropped on a spinning disc, the exam trap (a faster spin does not need a torque), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.

In this video:
0:00 Pull your arms in, spin faster: why?
0:24 Angular momentum L = I omega
0:46 Motion notebook: Diya on a spinning chair pulls two weights in
1:22 Slow-mo replay: a pull towards the axis has no torque
1:40 Why she speeds up, link by link
1:58 The rule in five steps: dL/dt = torque, I1 omega1 = I2 omega2
2:38 Arms out vs arms in + pause and think: spin energy
3:09 Pause and think: she lets go of the weights
3:29 Worked example: a ring dropped on a spinning disc
4:10 Exam trap: a faster spin without a torque
4:31 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:07 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Rolling Motion. A cycle wheel rolls down the road: its top races ahead, yet its bottom point is not moving at all. How?
